A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, methods and applications. All 22 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2 support comparison through readable text, equations, tables and figures. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original runtime experiments, synthetic clustering results, CIFAR10 distortion comparisons, and MNIST-based quantization and barycenter experiments in Table 1 and Figures 2–6.

after.justification: V2 retains original application experiments and reports additional runtime and convergence results in Tables 1–3, alongside revised synthetic clustering results.

M1.justification: The MSW, SMW and DSMW constructions, Algorithms 1–2, and DSMW quantization and barycenter optimization procedures are retained. The Gaussian-barycenter formula is mathematically corrected, but the PDFs do not describe a new construction or changed implementation.

E1.justification: Figure 2 replaces two four-mode synthetic populations with six-mode populations, extending cluster-number detection to another ground-truth cluster count. CIFAR10, MNIST and their application tasks remain unchanged. The larger runtime configurations are setting changes rather than new task coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds entropically regularized MW, computed using Sinkhorn iterations, to the actual runtime comparison in Table 1. V1 compares only MW, MSW and DSMW there. The application comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V2 revises the reported MSW stopping rule to average changes across component pairs, retaining the 10^-3 threshold and ten-iteration interval. It adds runtime configurations with 1,000–10,000 components at d=50 and dimensions 1,000–3,000 at K=10, and reports projection counts. The stopping-rule revision does not establish that retained timings were recomputed.

E4.justification: Tables 2–3 extend scaling analyses and examine how projection counts vary with component count and dimension. The entropic-MW comparison additionally tests whether accelerating the outer transport removes the runtime bottleneck. The retained barycenter images receive new discussion rather than a new experimental analysis.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly identifies the timing summaries as mean plus-minus standard deviation; v1 displays unexplained plus-minus values. The original ten-pair runtime setting is unchanged, and no increased repetition count, confidence interval or significance test is reported.

E6.justification: V2 substantially extends the central efficiency evidence with entropic-MW timings and new runtime/projection-count tables. For example, DSMW takes 0.16 seconds at d=50, K=10,000 and 6.90±3.21 seconds at d=3,000, K=10; MSW exceeds 60 seconds in both settings. Figure 2 adds six-cluster convergence outcomes. Original Table 1 timings and CIFAR10/MNIST result images are retained, so these are added results rather than same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Equation 3 replaces a linear Wasserstein/SW bound with exponent 1/[p(d+1)]. Theorem 3.2 consequently changes SMW ≤ C_P DSMW to SMW ≤ C_P DSMW^(1/6), with a revised proof using Jensen's inequality; Proposition 3.7 now bounds SW_2^6. V2 also corrects the moment definition and changes the Gaussian-barycenter formula from an unsquared Wasserstein objective to W_2 squared.

C1.justification: A central advertised theoretical guarantee is narrowed: the contribution schematic in Figure 1 replaces linear strong equivalence with 6-strong equivalence and the corresponding sixth-power SW bound. The conclusion also replaces preservation of geometric properties with reliance on Euclidean geometry. The proposed metric families and broad application claims remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains the practical compactness assumption and identifies unrestricted weak equivalence as conjectural. It adds interpretations of runtime bottlenecks and projection-count trends. For barycenters, it acknowledges loss of prominent input features and nearly unimodal intermediates, limits the toy example to computational feasibility, and interprets DSMW outputs as smoothed counterparts of SW point clouds.

D1.justification: V2 documents Sinkhorn regularization epsilon=0.1, explicitly states the clustering fit range k=2–9, and explains the ten-iteration stopping interval. It replaces v1's direct implementation repository link with a statement that code is supplementary and the repository will be available upon acceptance. That supplementary code is not contained in the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: The single-cell application citation changes from Yachimura et al. (2024) to Lin et al. (2023), which was already cited elsewhere, and the Yachimura reference is removed. Positioning relative to the independently developed Nguyen mixture-distance papers remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 separates Numerical Analysis from Experiments and Applications, moving the existing application subsections into Section 5 and the conclusion into Section 6. It adds localized explanations, standardizes mathematical notation, edits affiliation text and removes the acknowledgements. Most existing prose and narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a four-panel comparison, and Tables 2–3 add scaling displays. Figure 1 receives revised equivalence labels; Figure 2 replaces two examples and adds explanatory labeling; Figure 3 gains axis labels without changing its curves. Barycenter captions expand, while the remaining result imagery and overall visual organization are retained.

improvement.justification: The decisive gain is correction of an overstated central theoretical guarantee in Equation 3, Theorem 3.2 and Proposition 3.7, with a revised derivation. The entropic baseline, larger-scale timing evidence and explicit barycenter limitations also improve support and qualification of the conclusions. Removing the direct code link and introducing an unresolved citation placeholder reduce accessibility and polish, but do not outweigh these substantial scientific improvements.
